video.title: Everyone's Wrong About Instagram's New Logo

note: publishedTimeText is relative to the collection date (2026-10-12). Author names and @mentions removed.

comments.comment: 10 years ago I made a video when instagram redesigned their app icon. Who was watching back then?! Let me know. [link removed]
People will get used to it the same way they got used to the previous logos they initially hated too 😂

the thing with these hated redesigns is that they're all good designs, improvements, with clever thinking behind it, but they are still hated because of nostalgia, or because theyre a more boring version of the previous design
I'm currently in my 1st year for bachelor graphic design degree and I learned a few things from the video because I also liked this new design, but couldn't figure out why. Thanks for this.

I find it strange that everyone is obsessing over the R. I mean c'mon, everyone knows it says Instagram. The discussion I think we should be having is about the overall brand change which reflects the way the app has changed over the years. 

The old logo, like you said, was retro and so was the old app. You shared pics with family and friends and applied fun nostalgic filters and followed your besties. 

Today, we mindlessly scroll through a manufactured feed full of accounts we don't follow and probably don't want to see but can't seem to look away. Not to mention the endless ads. I think the new logo reflects this perfectly.
When I know it’s Instagram, I can read the R automatically. It looks good and clean, and also makes when u think of threads and meta logos.
I saw the new logotype and immediately thought, "Ooh! That's neat. I like the r."
It's a waste of time complaining about it when nobody using the app will be staring at this new logo. People will be too busy rotting their brains, doomscrolling through the slop to notice.
This was my take as well.  One additional point is that not only does the line thickness and curve restrictions match the IG logomark, but it also matches Threads and Meta too.
Also for me this new logo looks great and pairs really good with the icon. Thanks for making this so clear in your video.
Also its more balanced with the left side of the logo
I am a designer and I love the new logo...  I guess everyone needs to act as a pro in every single field these days and have extreme opinions about it online. One of the charms of social media

Great breakdown! The adjustment on that specific 'r' really changes the visual rhythm of the entire wordmark. It’s fascinating how a single letterform tweak makes such a huge impact on the overall perception.

IMO they could have tied the "r" to the "g" instead of the "a", like they did with the "n" and the "s", wich would have made it more legible. But other than that the new logo of course fits better to the Icon design.

I honestly don't know what the problem is.. A lot of people usually like following the band wagon really.. I don't think a lot of them know what they are even saying... A logo doesn't always have to be super legible, especially for an established brand... This is what makes them unique... Not everyone needs to spell out their brand name like Google.

The new word mark is actually fantastic. 
It's really unique in nature and the "r" makes complete the uniqueness. 
Those who don't get it, I am sure they are not used to change.
But branding is all about change.
The top right of the 'r' should be rounded!

Just FYI, the wordmark wasn't designed by Instagram's design team... There's a typeface designer at a well known, excellent firm who created the new wordmark. The info will be available to the public soon.

I don't think you should justify their already controversial decision. There was no need for a cursive 'r' to be there in the first place. If they really really wanted it.. they should have just made it connect with the g. How it's done feels like an unfinished draft. Also, it's something that you could have shown for how to improve the legibility keeping all of their new identity intact
Seeing you explain clearly helps me understand the choices it take to make the logotype that Instagram went for. Thanks a lot
+1, i was bewildered when dude said you dont need a logotype to be readable lmao. Accessibility shouldn't be sacrificed
Yes. Instagram is such a strong brand that it doesn't necessarily need an ultra legible logo imo
nope, look at the letter 't'

[@mention removed] same, this minimalist redesign wave is annoying. Lotta brands ruined their otherwise great logos
